clue.text: One's charges might be small, in more than one sense

definitions.text: One's charges might be small, in more than one sense

parts.words: One's charges might be small, in more than one sense
parts.note: the charges are young children in someone's care, small in size, and the fee charged for minding them is also small

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's fees are modest, with a hint of a second meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' reads first as fees, but it also means people placed in one's care; both senses are small here.
explanation.definitionFit: A person minding young children for a modest fee has small charges in both senses.

clue.text: Poetic gesture from beefcake, oddly

indicators.note: taking only the odd-numbered letters of the word beefcake, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A muscleman striking a strange pose in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like it describes the gesture, but it picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'beefcake'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beck is a summoning nod or wave, a word now found mostly in verse.

clue.text: Rod left with fish on

indicators.note: in a down entry, the fish placed on top of the other piece comes first

parts.note: a barbel is a freshwater fish with whiskery barbs at its mouth

explanation.surface: An angler's rod left lying with a fish still hooked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so BARBEL sits over L.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is a weightlifting bar, a type of rod with weights at each end.

clue.text: Act unconventionally to put one's life in order

indicators.note: putting these words in order means arranging their letters afresh into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Advice to sort out one's affairs and live more conventionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' seems to belong to the advice about tidying up a life, but it signals rearranging the letters of TO PUT ONES LIFE; the S of 'one's' counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate from accepted behaviour is the idiom's meaning, acting outside convention.

clue.text: Superior pub, mostly good for boozing

parts.note: top means superior, best

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A recommendation of a fine pub that is good for a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: Toping is an old word for drinking alcohol heavily, the same as boozing.

clue.text: Old friend, born in France, one taking the Baccalaurat?

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
ami is French for friend, the French setting carried over from 'in France'
née is French for born, used of a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A former friend, born in France, sitting the French school-leaving exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' serves both AMI and NEE as French words. The Baccalauréat is the French school-leaving exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting the French school-leaving exam is a candidate being tested.

clue.text: Order filling the books should make a fortune

indicators.note: one piece fills the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book, so two of them give BB
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Book-keeping advice that orders placed will earn a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a purchase order; it is the Order of Merit, a British honour, and B is the standard abbreviation for book.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: something that costs or earns a bomb costs or earns a great deal of money.

clue.text: Japanese location, satisfactory after a fashion, but ultimately deficient

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

indicators.note: missing its final letter, the last one lacking

parts.note: in a way means after a fashion, to some extent

explanation.surface: A place in Japan judged adequate in some respects but disappointing overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately deficient' seems a verdict on the place, but it removes the last letter of IN A WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is an island and prefecture in southern Japan.

clue.text: TV programme controller?

definitions.meaning: a reality television show in which housemates are watched constantly
the all-seeing ruler of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, a figure of state surveillance and control

explanation.surface: A question about who is in charge of a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: The reality show took its name from the dictator figure in Orwell's novel who watches and controls everyone.

clue.text: Aggressively overtake empty vehiole, riding on carriage

indicators.note: in an across entry, the pieces riding on the carriage come after it

parts.note: a car is a railway carriage

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse

explanation.surface: A driver aggressively passing an empty vehicle while riding on a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehiole' is an OCR misreading of 'vehicle'; its first and last letters are V and E either way. A jockey who is riding is said to be 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve someone up is British slang for cutting in sharply in front of them after overtaking.

clue.text: Energy shown by a mother is awesome

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
zing means liveliness or energy

explanation.surface: A mother showing energy wins admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that inspires wonder; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Listened to a sailor going over rough training ground

indicators.note: words that are listened to are heard, so the answer only sounds like them

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, and coarse means rough, so these say A SALT COARSE

explanation.surface: A sailor heard tramping over rough ground used for training.
explanation.walkthrough: A SALT COARSE, said aloud, sounds like the answer; 'going over' just joins the sailor to the rough.
explanation.definitionFit: An army obstacle circuit is a ground laid out for physical training.

clue.text: Situation that's difficult for some, and tacky for the rest?

definitions.text: Situation that's difficult for some, and tacky for the rest?

parts.words: Situation that's difficult for some, and tacky for the rest?
parts.note: a figurative tough position, and literally a board of tacks on which a fakir rests

explanation.surface: A situation that some find hard and others find in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tacky' reads as vulgar, but here it means full of tacks, and 'rest' is lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a painful situation, and it is literally a board studded with nails for lying on.

clue.text: Port's distinctive quality, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: an air is a distinctive quality or manner

explanation.surface: A remark on a port wine's distinctive character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the wine; it is a harbour town, and the 's stands for 'is'. AYR is a port on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a Scottish harbour town on the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: A writer's ballad mostly captured disastrous event

indicators.note: the writer has caught the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer; the 's stands for 'has'

indicators.note: most of the word, without its last letter

parts.note: a calypso is a West Indian song, a kind of ballad

explanation.surface: A writer's ballad, mostly about a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'writer's' stands for 'has', so the writer has captured the shortened ballad; a calypso is a Caribbean song.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a catastrophe on a vast scale, a disastrous event.

clue.text: Large number into physical exercises before a game

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, inside it
one piece placed before the other

parts.note: PE is physical education, physical exercises
a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of physical training before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: LOT goes into PE followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque ball game played against a wall, the source of jai alai.

clue.text: Etruscan rebels not submitting to authority

indicators.note: the letters of the word rebel against their order and form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ancient Etruscans rising up against a ruling power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' looks like a noun for the Etruscans, but it is a verb signalling that ETRUSCAN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A recusant refuses to submit to authority, historically a Catholic refusing Anglican services.

clue.text: Hotel cat sullied towel in kitchen

indicators.note: something sullied is spoiled and messed up, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A hotel cat dirties a towel in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cloth is a cloth for drying dishes, a towel used in a kitchen.

clue.text: What volunteer welfare worker gives, without worrying?

definitions.meaning: an unpaid welfare worker gives ..., at no charge

explanation.surface: A question about what an unpaid carer offers, without fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is care given free, which is what an unpaid welfare worker offers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untroubled by worries lives a life free of anxiety, an exact synonym.

clue.text: I'm gathering extremely reliable information about course of treatment

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
one piece goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
I'm gives its letters as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone gathering trustworthy facts about a medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' only links the pieces; the containment is signalled by 'about'. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication, a course of treatment.

clue.text: By the sound of it, a meal's relaxed

indicators.note: the answer is what these words sound like when spoken

parts.note: a tea is a meal, so a meal's gives A TEA'S

explanation.surface: Someone sounding relaxed after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea's, said aloud, matches the answer; tea is a meal in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command for standing relaxed is the same phrase meaning comfortable and untroubled.

clue.text: Land mass covered by a variety of heather

indicators.note: covered by the other piece, which surrounds it

parts.note: Erica is the genus of heaths and heathers
m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A stretch of land covered with a kind of heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land mass' reads as one phrase, but 'Land' is the definition and 'mass' gives M, which goes inside A + ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a country, and land can mean a nation or country.

clue.text: Having succeeded on racehorse, one looks quite happy

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded, as used in family trees
a miler is a horse that races over a mile

explanation.surface: A punter who has won with a horse looking pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts S above MILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiler is a person who smiles, someone looking pleased.

clue.text: No introduction needed for hit record

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to slog is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A hit record that needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit record' reads as a chart song, but 'hit' gives SLOG and 'record' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A log is a written record, such as a ship's log.

clue.text: Causes trouble to government department cutting wages

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, going inside it

parts.note: incomes are wages
MOD is the Ministry of Defence, a British government department

explanation.surface: A government department cutting pay causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: MOD, the UK Ministry of Defence, cuts into INCOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode someone is to inconvenience them, causing them trouble.

clue.text: Youngster forgetting first part of lesson is told off

indicators.note: forgetting something means it is left out of the word

parts.note: a child is a youngster

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A child who forgets the start of a lesson gets scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILD loses L, the first letter of 'lesson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chid is an old past tense of chide, meaning scolded or told off.

clue.text: Treat octogenarian initially for wind

parts.note: to pamper is to treat indulgently

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A treat for an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampero is a cold wind blowing across the South American pampas.

clue.text: Fairly big girl has come to grief

indicators.note: letters that come to grief are wrecked and end up in a new order

explanation.surface: A rather large girl has had an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' reads as the verb of the surface, but it is fodder with 'girl'; 'come to grief' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so the word means fairly big.

clue.text: Woman journalist put name to article

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A female reporter signing her name to a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Supervisor is given cards, following accusation

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, coming after it

parts.note: a charge is a formal accusation
a hand is the set of cards a player holds

explanation.surface: A supervisor dealt some cards after being accused.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a worker in charge of others, ranking below a foreman: a supervisor.
